questions.question: Which among following fundamental duties **is INCORRECT **related towards the protection and promotion of scientific and cultural values?

options.text: To develop the scientific temper, humanism and the spirit of inquiry and reform.
To safe guard the public property and to abjure violence
To strive towards excellence in all spheres of individual and collective activity.
To value and preserve the rich heritage of our composite culture.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To safe guard the public property and to abjure violence**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Fundamental Duties** are enshrined in **Part IV-A** of the **Constitution of India** under **Article 51A**. These duties were added to the constitution to remind citizens of their social and moral obligations towards the nation.
 
• **Article 51A(h)**: This clause states that it is the duty of every citizen **to develop the scientific temper, humanism and the spirit of inquiry and reform**. This duty is specifically designed to promote **scientific values** and **rational thinking** among the masses. Hence, this statement is correct.
 
• **Article 51A(f)**: This clause emphasizes the duty **to value and preserve the rich heritage of our composite culture**. This is the primary duty associated with the protection and promotion of **cultural values** and **historical legacy**. Hence, this statement is correct.
 
• **Article 51A(i)**: This clause mandates citizens **to safeguard public property and to abjure violence**. While this is a significant **Fundamental Duty**, it relates to **civic sense**, **law and order**, and **non-violence**, rather than the thematic category of **scientific** or **cultural values**. Hence, this statement is **incorrect** in the context of the specific theme mentioned in the question.
 
• **Article 51A(j)**: This clause encourages citizens **to strive towards excellence in all spheres of individual and collective activity** so that the nation constantly rises to higher levels of endeavor and achievement. While it promotes general progress, it is often grouped with duties that lead to **intellectual** and **cultural advancement**. Hence, this statement is correct.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Origin and Adoption**: The **Fundamental Duties** were not part of the original Constitution. They were incorporated based on the recommendations of the **Swaran Singh Committee** during the **Internal Emergency** in **1976**. The **42nd Amendment Act, 1976** introduced **10 duties** initially.
 
• **Source**: The concept of **Fundamental Duties** in the **Indian Constitution** was inspired by the constitution of the erstwhile **USSR** (now **Russia**). Unlike **Fundamental Rights**, these duties are **non-justiciable**, meaning they cannot be directly enforced by courts, though they serve as a guide for interpreting laws.
 
• **The 11th Duty**: Originally there were only **10** duties. The **11th Fundamental Duty**, which requires parents or guardians to provide opportunities for **education** to children between the **age** of **6 and 14 years**, was added by the **86th Constitutional Amendment Act** in the year **2002**.
 
• **Verma Committee (1999)**: This committee was established to identify the existence of legal provisions for the implementation of some of the **Fundamental Duties**. It pointed out that several duties are already enforceable through existing laws like the **Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act (1971)** and the **Protection of Civil Rights Act (1955)**.
 
• **Nature of Duties**: Some duties are **moral duties** (like cherishing the noble ideals of the freedom struggle), while others are **civic duties** (like respecting the **National Flag** and the **National Anthem**). They apply only to **citizens of India** and do not extend to **foreigners**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Significance of Scientific Temper**: The inclusion of **scientific temper** as a duty is unique to the **Indian Constitution**. It encourages a **questioning mind** and discourages **superstition**, aiming for a modern, progressive **India**.
 
• **Preservation of Culture**: The term **"Composite Culture"** refers to the **syncretic** and **diverse** traditions of **India**, including various **religions**, **languages**, and **ethnicities**, which citizens are expected to protect.
 
• **Public Property and Violence**: **Article 51A(i)** is crucial for maintaining **internal security** and **social harmony**, especially during protests or civil unrest, ensuring that **national assets** are not destroyed.

In this question, a question is followed by two statements numbered (I) and (II). You have to decide whether the data provided in the statements are sufficient to answer the question. Read both the statements and decide the appropriate answer.

Question:

Among 5 trees, L, M, N, T and V each having a different height, which tree is the shortest?

Statements:

(I) L is taller than only two trees. M is shorter than L and T is shorter than M.

(II) V is taller than N.

options.text: Data in Statement II alone is sufficient to answer the question while data in statement I is not
Both statements I and II together (and not statement 1 alone or statement II alone) are sufficient to answer the question
Data in Statement I alone is sufficient to answer the question while data in statement II is not
Both statements I and II together are NOT sufficient to answer the question

questions.solution:
Given Statements:

I. L is taller than only two trees. M is shorter than L and T is shorter than M.

II. V is taller than N.

Analysis:

I. From Statement I → L is taller than only two trees, so L is 3rd tallest.

Since, M is shorter than L and T is shorter than M, we get a definite order below L as L > M > T.

This already fixes T as the shortest among the given trees → **Statement I alone is sufficient.**

II. From Statement II → V is taller than N, but no relation with L, M, or T is given, so shortest cannot be determined → Not sufficient.

Using both I and II together → Although we can extend the ordering further, Statement I itself already identifies T as the shortest tree, so additional information is not required.

Hence, the correct answer is **Option 3.**

questions.question: The price of each article of type P, Q, and R is ₹280, ₹180 and ₹115, respectively. Rohit buys articles of each type in the ratio 4 : 2 : 7 for ₹6,855. How many articles of type Q did he purchase?

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

⇒ Ratio = 4 : 2 : 7 → total parts = 13

⇒ Cost of one ratio set = (4×280) + (2×180) + (7×115) = 2285

⇒ Number of sets = 6855 ÷ 2285 = 3

⇒ Q = 2 × 3 = 6

**∴ Answer = 6**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Total Cost = (Quantity × Price) + (Quantity × Price) + (Quantity × Price)

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let quantities be 4x, 2x, 7x

⇒ Total cost = (4x × 280) + (2x × 180) + (7x × 115)

⇒ = 1120x + 360x + 805x

⇒ = 2285x

⇒ 2285x = 6855

⇒ x = 3

⇒ Quantity of Q = 2x = 6

**∴ Final Answer = 6**

questions.question: Let ABC be a right-angled triangle such that ∠B = 90°. If tan A = 1, then find the value of cosec A sec A.

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

⇒ tan A = 1 ⇒ A = 45°

⇒ cosec A = √2, sec A = √2

⇒ cosec A × sec A = √2 × √2 = 2

**∴ Answer = 2**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

tan A = 1, ∠B = 90°

**Formula Used:**

tan A = Perpendicular / Base

cosec A = Hypotenuse / Perpendicular

sec A = Hypotenuse / Base

**Calculation:**

⇒ tan A = 1 ⇒ Perpendicular = Base

⇒ Let Perpendicular = 1, Base = 1

⇒ Hypotenuse = √(1² + 1²) = √2

⇒ cosec A = √2 / 1 = √2

⇒ sec A = √2 / 1 = √2

⇒ cosec A × sec A = √2 × √2 = 2

**∴ Final Answer = 2**

questions.question: Which of the following tabs in Task Manager shows CPU and memory usage graphs?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Performance**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Performance** tab in **Windows Task Manager** is specifically designed to provide real-time visualization of the **hardware resources** being utilized by the system.
 
• It displays dynamic **CPU (Central Processing Unit)** usage graphs, showing the current utilization percentage and **clock speed** (measured in **GHz**).
 
• This tab also provides detailed **memory usage graphs**, which track how much **RAM** (Random Access Memory) is currently in use, **available**, and **cached**.
 
• Beyond just CPU and RAM, the Performance tab monitors **Disk** activity (Read/Write speeds), **Ethernet/Wi-Fi** throughput (Send/Receive speeds), and **GPU** (Graphics Processing Unit) load.
 
• Users can view technical specifications such as the number of **Cores**, **Logical processors**, **L1/L2/L3 cache** sizes, and the system **Uptime** (the duration since the last **reboot**).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Startup Tab:**

 
 
• This tab manages applications that **automatically launch** when the **Windows** operating system starts.
 
• It helps users identify **Startup Impact**, which can be **High**, **Medium**, or **Low**, allowing them to disable unnecessary programs to speed up the **boot process**.
 
 
 
• **Users Tab:**
 
 
• This section lists all **active user accounts** currently logged into the **computer**.
 
• It provides a breakdown of resource consumption per user, which is essential for **administrators** managing **multi-user environments** or **servers**.
 
 
 
• **Details Tab:**
 
 
• The Details tab is an advanced version of the **Processes** tab, providing the **PID (Process ID)** for every running executable.
 
• It allows users to change **Process Priority** (e.g., High, Realtime) and set **CPU Affinity** to restrict a process to specific **processor cores**.
 
 
 
• **Processes Tab:**
 
 
• The primary tab that lists all **Apps**, **Background processes**, and **Windows processes** currently running.
 
• It is the main interface used to **End Task** for **frozen** or **non-responsive** applications.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Shortcuts:** The **Task Manager** can be quickly accessed by pressing **Ctrl + Shift + Esc** or by right-clicking the **Taskbar** in **Windows 10/11**.
 
• **Resource Monitor:** For more granular analysis, the Performance tab includes a link to the **Resource Monitor**, which offers **kernel-level** details about **disk I/O**, **network connections**, and **memory handles**.
 
• **Evolution:** While Task Manager has been a part of Windows since version **3.0**, the modern graphical interface with the Performance tab was significantly enhanced in **Windows 8** and **Windows 10**.
 
• **System Information:** The Performance tab is vital for **troubleshooting** hardware **bottlenecks** and identifying if the **CPU** is **throttling** or if the system is running out of **physical RAM**.

questions.question: Two parallel lines, L1 and L2, are cut by a transversal. If one of the interior angles on the same side of the transversal is 70°, what is the measure of the other interior angle on the same side of the transversal?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

⇒ Same-side interior angles in parallel lines are supplementary

⇒ Sum = 180°

⇒ Other angle = 180° − 70° = 110°

**∴ Answer = 110°**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Two parallel lines L1 and L2 with a transversal; one interior angle = 70°

**Formula Used:**

Same-side interior angles (co-interior angles) are supplementary

Sum = 180°

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let other angle = x

⇒ x + 70° = 180°

⇒ x = 180° − 70°

⇒ x = 110°

**∴ Final Answer = 110°**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

**Co-interior Angles:** Angles on same side of transversal sum to 180°

**Alternate Interior Angles:** Equal when lines are parallel

**Corresponding Angles:** Equal for parallel lines

**Linear Pair:** Adjacent angles forming a straight line sum to 180°

questions.question: In 2025, which organization released the Global Carbon Budget, providing the most comprehensive annual assessment of global carbon sources, sinks, and emission trends?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Global Carbon Project (GCP)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Global Carbon Project (GCP)** is an international research project that provides the most comprehensive annual assessment of the state of the global carbon cycle through its **Global Carbon Budget** report.
 
• The **Global Carbon Budget** tracks the trends in **global carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions**, including those from **fossil fuel combustion** and **land-use changes** such as **deforestation**.
 
• It quantifies the **carbon sinks**, which are the reservoirs that absorb carbon, including the **ocean** and **terrestrial biosphere** (land), to determine how much CO2 remains in the **atmosphere** each year.
 
• The data provided by the **GCP** is critical for monitoring progress toward the goals of the **Paris Agreement**, which aims to limit **global warming** to well below **2 degrees Celsius**, preferably **1.5 degrees Celsius**.
 
• The report is typically published in the peer-reviewed journal **Earth System Science Data** and involves a massive collaboration of over **100 scientists** from dozens of **international organizations**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC):**

 
 
• The **IPCC** is a **United Nations** body established in **1988** to assess the science related to **climate change**.

__
 
• The **Central Administrative Tribunal (CAT)** was established under **Article 323A** of the **Constitution of India**, which was inserted by the **42nd Amendment Act** in **1976**. • The **Administrative Tribunals Act, 1985**, specifically excludes certain categories from the jurisdiction of **CAT**. The selection is based on the recommendations of a **Search-cum-Selection Committee**, which is typically chaired by a **sitting Judge of the Supreme Court** who is nominated by the **Chief Justice of India (CJI)**, not the **Prime Minister**. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• The **CAT** is a multi-member body consisting of a **Chairman** and **Members** (both **Judicial** and **Administrative**). As of **2024**, the sanctioned strength of **Members** is **70** (including the **Chairman**).
 
• The **CAT** is not bound by the procedure laid down in the **Code of Civil Procedure, 1908**, but is guided by the **principles of natural justice**. This makes the process faster and less expensive for the aggrieved public servants.

Chandra Kumar case (1997)**, the **Supreme Court** ruled that the decisions of these tribunals are subject to the **writ jurisdiction** of the **High Courts** under **Article 226** and **Article 227**. questions.question: A hemispherical tank filled with water is being emptied through a pipe at a rate of 115.5 litres per second. If the tank has an internal radius of 31.5 m, determine the time required to drain 50% of the tank's water. (Use pi = (22)/(7))

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question: What type of activity is tourism classified as?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tertiary**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Tourism is classified as a **Tertiary** activity because it is essentially a service-oriented industry. Unlike the primary or secondary sectors, it does not produce a tangible physical product but instead provides experiences and services to consumers.
 
• It involves a wide range of services including **Transportation** (airlines, railways, road transport), **Accommodation** (hotels, resorts, homestays), **Catering** (restaurants, cafes), and **Entertainment** (theme parks, museums, guided tours).
 
• Economic impact: Tourism is a major contributor to the **Global Gross Domestic Product (GDP)**. According to reports from the **World Travel and Tourism Council (WTTC)**, the sector accounted for approximately **9.1%** of the world **GDP** in **2023**, showing a robust recovery post-pandemic.
 
• Employment generation: As a **Tertiary** activity, tourism is highly labor-intensive. It creates direct employment for **Tour Guides**, **Travel Agents**, and **Hotel Staff**, and indirect employment in sectors like **Handicrafts** and **Local Transport**.
 
• Tourism acts as an **Invisible Export**. When international tourists visit a **Country**, they spend **Foreign Exchange** on local services, which improves the **Balance of Payments** of the host nation without the physical movement of goods across borders.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Primary Sector**: This involves the direct extraction or harvest of natural resources from the earth. Examples include **Agriculture**, **Mining**, **Fishing**, and **Forestry**. These activities are foundational to the economy.
 
• **Secondary Sector**: This sector focuses on the transformation of raw materials into finished goods through **Manufacturing** and **Construction**. For instance, converting cotton into cloth or iron ore into steel falls under this category.
 
• **Quaternary Sector**: This is a subset of the tertiary sector that is knowledge-based. It includes services such as **Information Technology (IT)**, **Research and Development (R&D)**, **Financial Planning**, and **Consultancy**. It is driven by intellectual capital.
 
• **Quinary Sector**: This represents the highest level of decision-making in a society or economy. It includes top executives and officials in **Government**, **Science**, **Universities**, and **Healthcare** who make key policy decisions.
 
• The classification of these activities helps in understanding the **Economic Structure** of a country. Developed nations typically have a higher percentage of their **Workforce** employed in the **Tertiary** and **Quaternary** sectors.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Tourism in India**: In **India**, tourism is a vital sector managed by the **Ministry of Tourism**. It plays a significant role in **Foreign Exchange Earnings (FEE)**. In the year **2023**, **India** saw a significant rise in **Foreign Tourist Arrivals (FTAs)** compared to the previous **two years**.
 
• **Government Initiatives**: The **Government of India** launched the **Swadesh Darshan Scheme** and the **PRASHAD Scheme** (Pilgrimage Rejuvenation and Spiritual Augmentation Drive) to develop thematic tourism circuits and infrastructure at pilgrimage sites.
 
• **Global Statistics**: The **United Nations World Tourism Organization (UNWTO)**, headquartered in **Madrid**, **Spain**, tracks global travel data. They reported that international tourist arrivals reached **1.3 billion** globally in **2023**, nearing **88%** of pre-pandemic levels.
 
• **Sustainable Tourism**: Modern tourism focuses on **Ecotourism** and sustainable practices to minimize the environmental footprint. This includes the conservation of **Biodiversity** and respecting the **Cultural Heritage** of local communities.

questions.question: Which 13th-century 1193 CE monument was built by Qutb-ud-din Aibak?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Quwwatul Islam Masjid**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Quwwat-ul-Islam Mosque** (translated as 'Might of Islam') was commissioned by **Qutb-ud-din Aibak**, the founder of the **Mamluk (Slave) Dynasty**, in the year **1193 CE**.
 
• It is historically significant as the **first mosque** built in **Delhi** after the Islamic conquest of **India** and serves as a primary example of **Indo-Islamic architecture**.
 
• The mosque is located within the **Qutb Complex** in **Mehrauli**, **South Delhi**, which is currently a **UNESCO World Heritage Site** (designated in **1993**).
 
• The construction of the mosque was carried out using the materials and spoils from **27 Hindu and Jain temples** that were demolished during the expansion of the **Ghurid Empire**.
 
• Architecturally, the mosque features a large **rectangular courtyard** (measuring **43m by 33m**) surrounded by **cloisters**, and its prayer hall is adorned with five **corbelled arches** carved with **floral patterns** and **Quranic inscriptions**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Qutub Minar:**

 
 
• While also initiated by **Qutb-ud-din Aibak**, the construction of this **73-meter** high victory tower began later, around **1199 CE**.
 
• Aibak only completed the **first storey**; the subsequent three storeys were added by his successor, **Iltutmish**, in **1220**, and the final storey was repaired/added by **Firoz Shah Tughlaq** in **1368**.
 
• It was built to honor the **Sufi saint** **Qutbuddin Bakhtiar Kaki**.
 
 
 
• **Red Fort (Lal Qila):**
 
 
• This monument was not built in the **13th century**; it was commissioned by the Mughal Emperor **Shah Jahan** in **1639** when he decided to shift his capital from **Agra** to **Shahjahanabad** (Old Delhi).
 
• It is made of **red sandstone** and represents the zenith of **Mughal architecture**, blending **Persian**, **Timurid**, and **Indian** styles.
 
 
 
• **Jama Masjid:**
 
 
• The **Jama Masjid** of **Delhi** is one of the largest mosques in **India**, built by **Shah Jahan** between **1650 and 1656**.
 
• It is located opposite the **Red Fort** and was constructed at a cost of **1 million rupees** at that time.
 
 
 
• **Qutb-ud-din Aibak:**
 
 
• He was originally a **Turkic slave** and the most trusted general of **Mu'izz ad-Din Muhammad Ghori**.
 
• He served as the **Sultan of Delhi** from **1206 to 1210** and is known as **Lakh Baksh** (Giver of Lakhs) due to his **generosity**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **Quwwat-ul-Islam Mosque** underwent several expansions; **Iltutmish** doubled the size of the prayer hall in **1230**, and **Alauddin Khalji** added the **Alai Darwaza** (gateway) and intended to build the **Alai Minar** in the **14th century**.
 
• Within the courtyard of the mosque stands the **Iron Pillar**, which dates back to the **4th century CE** (Gupta Period) and is famous for its **rust-resistant** properties, standing as a testament to **ancient Indian metallurgy**.
 
• The transition from **Hindu-temple craftsmanship** to **Islamic architectural forms** is visible in the mosque's **screens**, where local artisans used **traditional stone-cutting techniques** to create **Arabic calligraphy** and **geometric designs**.

questions.question: Providing free legal aid under Article 39A indirectly promotes which Preamble objective?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Justice**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 39A** of the **Constitution of India** mandates that the State shall secure that the operation of the legal system promotes **justice** on a basis of equal opportunity.
 
• It specifically directs the State to provide **free legal aid** by suitable legislation or schemes to ensure that opportunities for securing **justice** are not denied to any citizen by reason of economic or other disabilities.
 
• The **Preamble** of the Indian Constitution explicitly lists **Justice**—**social, economic, and political**—as the first of its core objectives for all citizens.
 
• By providing legal assistance to those who cannot afford it, **Article 39A** acts as a practical mechanism to achieve the **social and economic justice** promised in the **Preamble**. ***Hence, the statement regarding Justice is correct.***
 
• This provision ensures that the **Rule of Law** is maintained and that the legal system does not become a tool only for the wealthy, thereby promoting **egalitarianism**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Constitutional Background:**

 
 
• **Article 39A** was not part of the original Constitution; it was inserted by the **42nd Amendment Act** in **1976** during the **Emergency**.
 
• This amendment is often referred to as the **"Mini-Constitution"** due to the vast number of changes it introduced to the **Indian Constitution**.
 
 
 
• **Legal Framework:**
 
 
• To give effect to **Article 39A**, the **Legal Services Authorities Act** was enacted in **1987**.
 
• This **Act** led to the establishment of the **National Legal Services Authority (NALSA)** to monitor and evaluate the implementation of legal aid programs.
 
• It also established **State Legal Services Authorities** and **District Legal Services Authorities** to provide **free legal services** at the grassroots level.
 
 
 
• **Other Preamble Objectives:**
 
 
• **Sovereignty:** Refers to the independent authority of the **State**, meaning it is not under the control of any external power. While vital, it is not directly promoted by legal aid.
 
• **Republic:** Indicates that the **Head of State** (the **President**) is elected and not a hereditary monarch.
 
• **Secularism:** Implies that the **State** has no official religion and treats all religions equally. Legal aid is provided regardless of religion, but its primary target is **Justice**.
 
 
 
• **Beneficiaries of Free Legal Aid:**
 
 
• Eligible groups include members of **Scheduled Castes (SC)** and **Scheduled Tribes (ST)**, **women**, **children**, **victims of human trafficking**, **disabled persons**, and individuals with an **annual income** below a specified limit (which varies by state).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Judicial Contribution:** The concept of **legal aid** was significantly championed by **Justice V.R. Krishna Iyer** and **Justice P.N. Bhagwati**, who emphasized that legal aid is a fundamental aspect of **Article 21** (Right to Life and Personal Liberty).
 
• **Lok Adalats:** Under the **1987 Act**, **Lok Adalats** were given statutory status. They serve as an alternative dispute resolution mechanism to provide **speedy and cost-effective justice**, further supporting the goal of **Article 39A**.
 
• **International Context:** The provision of **free legal aid** aligns with **Article 7** and **Article 8** of the **Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR)**, which advocate for equality before the law and the right to an effective remedy.
 
• **Constitutional Linkage:** **Article 39A** is a **Directive Principle of State Policy (DPSP)**. While **DPSPs** are non-justiciable in court, they are fundamental in the governance of the **country**, and the **State** is duty-bound to apply these principles when making laws.

questions.question: Which tab in the Windows 11 Task Manager allows a user to change the priority of a running application?'
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Details**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Task Manager** in **Windows 11** is a powerful system monitor and management utility that provides information about the processes and programs running on a computer.
 
• The **Details** tab is the specific section where users can see a detailed list of all active processes, including their **Process ID (PID)**, **Status**, **User Name**, **CPU usage**, and **Memory** footprint.
 
• By right-clicking a process in the **Details** tab, a user can access the **"Set priority"** menu. This allows the user to allocate more or fewer **CPU cycles** to a specific application relative to other running tasks. ***Hence, this option is correct.***
 
• There are six priority levels available: **Realtime**, **High**, **Above Normal**, **Normal**, **Below Normal**, and **Low**. Changing these settings can help optimize performance for **resource-intensive** tasks like **video editing** or **gaming**.
 
• Unlike the general "Processes" tab which groups tasks, the **Details** tab provides a granular view of every **.exe** file executing in the **Windows environment**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Performance Tab:**

 
 
• This tab provides real-time **graphical representations** of the system's hardware utilization.
 
• It monitors the **Central Processing Unit (CPU)**, **Random Access Memory (RAM)**, **Disk (HDD/SSD)**, **Ethernet**, **Wi-Fi**, and **Graphics Processing Unit (GPU)**.
 
• While it is excellent for diagnosing **bottlenecks**, it does not provide the functionality to change individual process priorities. ***Hence, this statement/option is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Startup Apps Tab:**
 
 
• Previously located in **msconfig**, this tab manages programs that launch automatically during the **boot process**.
 
• Users can **Enable** or **Disable** apps to improve the **startup speed** of the **Windows 11** operating system.
 
• It measures the **"Startup impact"** of each application but does not manage the runtime priority of currently active apps. ***Hence, this statement/option is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Users Tab:**
 
 
• This tab displays the resources being consumed by each **User Account** currently logged into the **PC**.
 
• It is particularly useful in **multi-user environments** or **servers** to see if a specific user is consuming excessive **bandwidth** or **processing power**.
 
• It allows a user to **Disconnect** or **Log off** other users but does not offer priority adjustment for individual processes. ***Hence, this statement/option is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Processes Tab:**
 
 
• This is the default tab that opens in **Task Manager**. It provides a high-level summary of **Apps**, **Background processes**, and **Windows processes**.
 
• While you can **End Task** here, the option to "Set priority" was moved to the **Details** tab in later versions of **Windows** to prevent accidental system instability.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Administrative Privileges:** To change the priority of certain **system-level processes** or processes owned by other users, the **Task Manager** must be running with **Administrator rights**.
 
• **Realtime Priority Risk:** Setting a process to **Realtime** priority is generally discouraged. It can cause the **OS** to prioritize that app over essential **input/output** drivers (like the **mouse** or **keyboard**), potentially leading to a **system freeze**.
 
• **CPU Affinity:** In the **Details** tab, users can also set **"CPU Affinity,"** which restricts a process to specific **CPU cores**. This is useful for older **software** that crashes on **multi-core** processors.
 
• **Keyboard Shortcut:** The fastest way to open the **Task Manager** in any **Windows** version is by pressing **Ctrl + Shift + Esc**.

questions.question: Which of the following regions would you expect has the highest population density based on geographic factors?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ganga River basin in India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Ganga River basin** in **India** is one of the most densely populated regions in the world due to its fertile **alluvial soil** and abundant **water availability**. It supports intensive **agriculture**, which sustains a massive population. ***Hence, this option is correct.***
 
• The **Amazon rainforest** in **Brazil** (**South America**) is characterized by a **hot and humid climate** with extremely dense vegetation. These geographical constraints make the area difficult for large-scale human settlement, resulting in very low **population density**. ***Hence, this statement is incorrect.***
 
• The **Sahara Desert** in **Africa** is the world's largest hot desert, where extreme **aridity**, high temperatures, and lack of **permanent water sources** make most of the region uninhabitable. Population is concentrated only in small **oases**. ***Hence, this statement is incorrect.***
 
• The **Canadian Arctic tundra** is located in the high latitudes of **North America**. The presence of **permafrost**, extremely **low temperatures**, and a short growing season prevent **agriculture** and infrastructure development, leading to sparse populations. ***Hence, this statement is incorrect.***
 
• Geographically, **river valleys** and **plains** like the **Ganga-Brahmaputra basin** traditionally host higher densities (often exceeding **1,000 persons per sq km**) compared to mountains, deserts, or thick forests.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Ganga River System:**

 
 
• The river originates from the **Gangotri Glacier** as the **Bhagirathi** and flows for approximately **2,525 km** through **India** and **Bangladesh**.
 
• In **India**, it covers the states of **Uttarakhand**, **Uttar Pradesh**, **Bihar**, and **West Bengal**, which are among the most populous states as per the **2011 Census**.
 
• The basin provides **irrigation** for crops like **rice**, **wheat**, and **sugarcane**, acting as the "food bowl" of the nation.
 
 
 
• **Factors Influencing Population Density:**
 
 
• **Topography:** People prefer living on **flat plains** rather than **mountains** or **plateaus** because these areas are suitable for **farming**, **manufacturing**, and **service activities**.
 
• **Climate:** Extreme climates (too hot or too cold) like the **Sahara** or **Russian Tundra** are avoided. Moderate **Monsoon climates** favor high density.
 
• **Soil Fertility:** Areas with fertile **alluvial** or **volcanic soils** provide agricultural productivity, naturally attracting more people.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Global Comparisons:** Apart from the **Ganga basin**, other high-density river basins include the **Huang He** and **Chang Jiang** in **China** and the **Nile** in **Egypt**.
 
• **Economic Impact:** The high **population density** in the **Ganga basin** has led to rapid **urbanization** and the growth of industrial hubs like **Kanpur**, **Varanasi**, and **Kolkata**.
 
• **Environmental Challenges:** High density in these fertile regions often leads to **pollution** and depletion of **groundwater** resources, necessitating government schemes like **Namami Gange** (launched in **2014**) for conservation.

questions.question: Which of the following was a function of the Vaishya class in later Vedic society?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Producing class**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the **Later Vedic Period** (circa **1000 BCE – 600 BCE**), the **Vaishya** varna was designated as the **producing class**. They were primarily responsible for the economic sustenance of the society through activities like **agriculture**, **cattle-rearing**, and **commerce**. *Hence, the statement regarding their function as the producing class is correct.*
 
• The **Vaishyas** evolved from the **Rig Vedic** term **"Vis,"** which referred to the common mass of the people. While the **Brahmanas** were ritual specialists and the **Kshatriyas** were the ruling/warrior class, the **Vaishyas** formed the bulk of the population involved in **productive labor**.
 
• They were the only varna among the three higher orders that acted as **tribute-payers** (**Balikrita**). The wealth generated by the **Vaishyas** through **trade** and **farming** supported the administrative needs of the **Kshatriyas** and the religious functions of the **Brahmanas**.
 
• During this era, **Vaishyas** held the status of **Dvija** (twice-born), which granted them the right to the **Upanayana** (sacred thread ceremony) and the study of the **Vedas**, distinguishing them from the **Shudra** class.
 
• The **Shatapatha Brahmana** and **Aitareya Brahmana** provide significant details about their social standing, often describing them as being "oppressed at will" or "tributary to others," indicating a growing social gap between them and the ruling elite.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Transition to Settled Agriculture**: The **Later Vedic Period** marked a major shift from a **pastoral economy** to a **sedentary agricultural** society. This transition took place largely in the **Upper Gangetic Basin** (modern-day **Uttar Pradesh** and **Haryana**), facilitated by the use of **iron implements** (**Shyama Ayas**) for clearing dense forests.
 
• **Varna Hierarchy**:
 
 
• **Brahmanas**: Occupied the highest rank; their **functions** included performing **sacrifices** (**Yajnas**) and preserving **Vedic knowledge**.
 
• **Kshatriyas**: The **ruling class**; their **features** included protection of the community, administration, and warfare.
 
• **Shudras**: The **subordinated class**; their **applications** were limited to serving the three higher varnas, and they were excluded from **Vedic rituals**.
 
 
 
• **Economic Specialization**: As **surplus production** grew, **Vaishyas** increasingly engaged in **internal and external trade**. Guilds began to form, and terms like **Shresthin** (head of a guild) started appearing in texts, signifying the growing **financial power** of the merchant class.
 
• **Geographic Location**: The center of **Vedic civilization** shifted from the **Sapta-Sindhu** region to the **Kuru-Panchala** region (Western **India** and the **Ganga-Yamuna Doab**), where the **Vaishya** communities established stable agricultural villages.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Social Status and Religion**: Despite being the **economic backbone**, the **Vaishyas** faced social restrictions. This dissatisfaction later became a catalyst for the rise of **Jainism** and **Buddhism** in the **6th Century BCE**, as these new faiths provided **merchants** and **traders** a higher social status regardless of their birth.
 
• **Taxation and State**: The concept of a structured **taxation system** emerged, where the **Vaishya** contributed a portion of their **grain** and **cattle** to the **King** (**Rajan**) as **Bali** or **Shulka**. This transition from voluntary gifts to mandatory taxes helped in the formation of early **territorial states** (**Janapadas**).
 
• **Literary Evidence**: The **Later Vedic texts**, including the **Samaveda**, **Yajurveda**, and **Atharvaveda**, along with the **Brahmanas** and **Upanishads**, provide the primary **data** regarding the **division of labor** and the specific **functions** of the **Vaishya** varna.

questions.question: What is the green pigment found in plants that is essential for capturing light energy during photosynthesis?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chlorophyll**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Chlorophyll** is the primary **green pigment** found in the **chloroplasts** of plants, algae, and cyanobacteria, and it is vital for the process of **photosynthesis**. It allows plants to absorb energy from **light**, primarily in the **blue** and **red** portions of the electromagnetic spectrum. ***Hence, Option A is correct.***
 
• **Hemoglobin** is a complex protein found in the **red blood cells** (erythrocytes) of humans and other vertebrates. Its primary function is to transport **oxygen** from the lungs to the body tissues and return **carbon dioxide** from the tissues back to the lungs. It contains **Iron (Fe)** rather than the pigments used by plants. ***Hence, Option B is incorrect.***
 
• **Insulin** is a peptide **hormone** produced by the **beta cells** of the **pancreas**. It plays a crucial role in regulating **carbohydrate and fat metabolism** in the body by promoting the absorption of **glucose** from the blood into liver, fat, and skeletal muscle cells. It is not a pigment. ***Hence, Option C is incorrect.***
 
• **Glucose** (**C6H12O6**) is a **simple sugar** (monosaccharide) that serves as the primary **source of energy** for living organisms. While it is a product of **photosynthesis**, it is a chemical compound and not a light-capturing pigment. ***Hence, Option D is incorrect.***
 
• The **location** of chlorophyll is within the **thylakoid membranes** of the **chloroplast**. These membranes are stacked into structures called **grana**, where the **Light-Dependent Reactions** of photosynthesis occur.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Chemical Structure of Chlorophyll:** The molecule consists of a **porphyrin ring** (similar to the heme group in hemoglobin) but with a **Magnesium (Mg)** atom at its center. It also possesses a long **hydrocarbon tail** (phytol chain) that anchors the molecule to the **thylakoid membrane**.
 
• **Types of Chlorophyll:** There are several types, but **Chlorophyll a** and **Chlorophyll b** are the most common in terrestrial plants. **Chlorophyll a** is the **primary pigment** involved in **light reactions**, while **Chlorophyll b** acts as an **accessory pigment**, broadening the range of light a plant can use by transferring energy to chlorophyll a.
 
• **Discovery:** Chlorophyll was first isolated and named by **Joseph Bienaimé Caventou** and **Pierre-Joseph Pelletier** in the year **1817**. This discovery laid the foundation for modern **plant physiology**.
 
• **Photosynthesis Process:** The process is divided into two stages: the **Light-Dependent Reactions** (where chlorophyll captures solar energy to produce **ATP** and **NADPH**) and the **Light-Independent Reactions** (also known as the **Calvin Cycle**, where **carbon dioxide** is fixed into **glucose**).
 
• **Applications:** Beyond its biological role, chlorophyll is used as a **food additive (E140)** for green coloring, in **cosmetics**, and in **alternative medicine** due to its perceived antioxidant properties.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Chlorosis:** This is a condition in plants where leaves produce insufficient chlorophyll. This often results from a **nutrient deficiency** of **Magnesium** or **Nitrogen**, or poor soil **pH** levels. Without enough chlorophyll, the plant's **growth rate** decreases significantly.
 
• **Absorption vs. Reflection:** Chlorophyll appears green because it **reflects** green light (wavelengths around **500–570 nm**) while **absorbing** the energy-rich blue and red light. This is why **LED grow lights** often use a combination of red and blue bulbs to maximize **efficiency**.
 
• **Comparison with Hemoglobin:** A fascinating **feature** of nature is the structural similarity between **chlorophyll** and **hemoglobin**. While chlorophyll uses **Magnesium** to help plants create energy from light, hemoglobin uses **Iron** to help animals transport oxygen through the **bloodstream**.
 
• **Accessory Pigments:** Apart from chlorophyll, plants also contain **Carotenoids** (orange) and **Xanthophylls** (yellow). These pigments become visible in the **autumn** season when chlorophyll breaks down due to **colder temperatures** and shorter **daylight hours**.

questions.question: As per Article 243Y of the Indian Constitution, to whom does the Finance Commission submit its recommendations regarding Municipalities?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Governor of the State**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 243Y** of the **Constitution of India** specifically deals with the **Finance Commission** in the context of **Municipalities**. It mandates that the **Finance Commission** constituted under **Article 243-I** shall also review the financial position of the **Municipalities** and make recommendations to the **Governor of the State**.
 
• The **Finance Commission** makes recommendations to the **Governor** regarding the distribution between the **State** and the **Municipalities** of the net proceeds of the taxes, duties, tolls, and fees leviable by the **State**, which may be divided between them under this **Part IXA**.
 
• The **Commission** also recommends the principles which should govern the determination of the taxes, duties, tolls, and fees which may be assigned to, or appropriated by, the **Municipalities**.
 
• It provides suggestions on the **grants-in-aid** to the **Municipalities** from the **Consolidated Fund of the State** and measures needed to improve the financial position of the **Municipalities**.
 
• The **Governor** is required to cause every recommendation made by the **Commission** under **Article 243Y**, together with an explanatory memorandum as to the action taken thereon, to be laid before the **Legislature of the State**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **74th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992**: This landmark legislation, which came into effect on **June 1, 1993**, granted constitutional status to **urban local bodies** (Municipalities). It added **Part IXA** (The Municipalities) and the **Twelfth Schedule** to the **Indian Constitution**.
 
• **Twelfth Schedule**: This schedule contains **18 functional items** that fall under the jurisdiction of **Municipalities**, including **urban planning**, **regulation of land use**, **construction of buildings**, **roads and bridges**, **public health**, and **sanitation**.
 
• **Types of Municipalities**: The **Constitution** provides for three types of municipalities: **Nagar Panchayat** for a transitional area (from rural to urban), **Municipal Council** for a smaller urban area, and **Municipal Corporation** for a larger urban area.
 
• **Article 243-I**: While **Article 243Y** concerns **Municipalities**, **Article 243-I** mandates the constitution of a **State Finance Commission** every **five years** by the **Governor** to review the financial position of **Panchayats**. The same commission typically handles both **Panchayats** and **Municipalities**.
 
• **Composition and Tenure**: The **State Legislature** may provide for the composition of the **Finance Commission**, the qualifications for members, and the manner of their selection. Typically, these commissions are constituted every **5 years** to ensure continuous fiscal monitoring.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Central Finance Commission (Article 280)**: Distinct from the **State Finance Commission**, the **President of India** constitutes a **Finance Commission** every **five years** under **Article 280**. It makes recommendations on the distribution of tax proceeds between the **Union** and the **States**.
 
• **State Finance Commission (SFC) Functions**: The **SFC** acts as a fiscal intermediary to ensure that **local bodies** have sufficient resources to perform their functions. It reviews the financial status and suggests ways to augment the **Consolidated Fund of a State** to supplement the resources of the **Municipalities**.
 
• **Role of the Governor**: As the **Constitutional Head** of the **State**, the **Governor** plays a pivotal role in the decentralization process by appointing the **Commission** and ensuring its reports reach the **State Assembly** for legislative action.
 
• **Financial Autonomy**: Provisions like **Article 243Y** are essential for the **financial autonomy** of **local governments**, allowing them to fund essential services like **solid waste management**, **street lighting**, and **water supply** without being entirely dependent on **State Government** discretion.

questions.question: India adopted the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) in which year?
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **September 2015**, **India** along with **192** other member states of the **United Nations**, officially adopted the **2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development**. This transformative plan aims to address global challenges including poverty, inequality, and climate change.
 
• The **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)** consist of **17 Goals** and **169** associated **targets** that are integrated and indivisible, balancing the three dimensions of sustainable development: economic, social, and environmental.
 
• The **United Nations Sustainable Development Summit**, held in **New York** from **September 25 to 27, 2015**, served as the platform for this historic agreement, succeeding the **Millennium Development Goals (MDGs)**.
 
• The implementation period for these goals began on **1 January 2016** and is set to conclude in the **year 2030**. This timeframe provides a **15-year** window for **countries** to mobilize efforts to end all forms of poverty.
 
• In **India**, the **NITI Aayog** (National Institution for Transforming India) has been assigned the role of the nodal agency to oversee the implementation of the **SDGs** and to ensure that all **ministries** and **states** align their policies with these global targets.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **SDG India Index:** To measure progress at the sub-national level, **NITI Aayog** launched the first edition of the **SDG India Index** in **December 2018**. It ranks **states** and **Union Territories** based on their performance across various indicators, promoting competitive federalism.
 
• **Core Goals:** Some of the prominent goals include **Goal 1 (No Poverty)**, **Goal 2 (Zero Hunger)**, **Goal 5 (Gender Equality)**, and **Goal 13 (Climate Action)**. These **functions** as a universal call to action to protect the planet and ensure peace.
 
• **Monitoring Framework:** The **Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI)** developed the **National Indicator Framework (NIF)**, which uses **data** and **statistical values** to track **India's** progress toward the **targets** periodically.
 
• **Voluntary National Review (VNR):** **India** presented its first **VNR** report to the **United Nations High-Level Political Forum (HLPF)** in **2017** and a second one in **2020**, highlighting the **country's** strategies for achieving the **2030 Agenda**.
 
• **Global Context:** Unlike the **MDGs**, which were primarily focused on developing **countries**, the **SDGs** are universal and apply to all **nations** regardless of their wealth or development status.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The concept of the **SDGs** was born at the **United Nations Conference on Sustainable Development**, also known as **Rio+20**, held in **Rio de Janeiro**, **Brazil**, in **June 2012**.
 
• The motto of the **SDGs** is **"Leave No One Behind,"** which emphasizes reaching the most vulnerable populations in every **location** and **community**.
 
• Significant government schemes in **India** like **Swachh Bharat Mission**, **Beti Bachao Beti Padhao**, and **Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana** are directly mapped to specific **SDG goals** to accelerate their achievement.
 
• The **targets** involve specific **numerical values** and **dates**; for **example**, **Target 1.1** aims to eradicate extreme poverty for all people everywhere by **2030**, currently measured as people living on less than **$2.15** a **day**.

questions.question: On which of the following National Waterways of India is the floating terminal Farakka situated?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**National Waterways 1**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **National Waterway 1 (NW-1)** spans the **Ganga-Bhagirathi-Hooghly** river system and is the longest waterway in **India**, covering a total distance of **1,620 km**.
 
• The waterway connects **Prayagraj (Allahabad)** in **Uttar Pradesh** to **Haldia** in **West Bengal**, passing through major cities like **Varanasi**, **Patna**, and **Munger**.
 
• The **Farakka** floating terminal is a significant infrastructure point located on **NW-1** in the **Murshidabad district** of **West Bengal**. It facilitates the movement of cargo through the **Farakka Barrage** and navigation lock.
 
• **NW-1** was declared a National Waterway in **October 1986** and is managed by the **Inland Waterways Authority of India (IWAI)**, headquartered in **Noida**.
 
• This waterway is vital for the transport of bulk goods such as **coal**, **fertilizers**, **cement**, and **food grains**, significantly reducing logistics costs compared to road or rail transport.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• This waterway is located on the **Brahmaputra River** in **Assam**, stretching **891 km** between **Sadiya** and **Dhubri**.
 
• It was declared in **1988** and serves as a major transport route for the **North Eastern** states of India.
 
 
 
• **National Waterway 3 (NW-3):**
 
 
• Also known as the **West Coast Canal**, it is located in **Kerala** and runs from **Kottapuram** to **Kollam** over a distance of **205 km**.
 
• It was the first National Waterway in India to offer **24-hour navigation** facilities throughout its entire length.
 
 
 
• **National Waterway 5 (NW-5):**
 
 
• This waterway comprises the **Brahmani River**, **Mahanadi delta rivers**, and the **East Coast Canal**, covering **623 km** across **Odisha** and **West Bengal**.
 
• It is crucial for transporting **minerals** and **industrial products** from the hinterlands of **Odisha** to the ports.
 
 
 
• **National Waterways Act, 2016:**
 
 
• This legislation increased the number of declared National Waterways in **India** from 5 to **111** to promote inland water transport as a fuel-efficient and environment-friendly mode.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Jal Marg Vikas Project (JMVP):**

• The estimated cost of the project is approximately **Rs. 5,369 crore**, aiming to enable the navigation of vessels with a capacity of **1,500 to 2,000 tonnes**.
 
• Under this project, **Multi-modal Terminals (MMTs)** have been constructed at **Varanasi** (UP), **Sahibganj** (Jharkhand), and **Haldia** (WB).
 
 
 
• **Farakka Navigation Lock:**

• The **Farakka** region serves as a strategic gateway for **Indo-Bangladesh Protocol (IBP)** routes, enhancing international trade via waterways.

questions.question: Which physical quantity can be zero even when a body is in motion?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Displacement**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Displacement** is defined as the **shortest distance** between the **initial position** and the **final position** of an object. Since it depends only on the endpoints, if an object moves and returns to its original starting point, the net **displacement** will be **zero**. ***Hence, the statement regarding Displacement is correct.***
 
• **Distance** refers to the **total path length** traveled by an object during its motion. Because path length is cumulative and does not depend on direction, it can never be **zero** as long as the body has moved from its position. ***Hence, the statement regarding Distance is incorrect.***
 
• **Speed** is a **scalar quantity** calculated as the total distance divided by the total time taken. Since distance for a moving body is always a **positive numerical value**, the speed of a body in motion can never be **zero**. ***Hence, the statement regarding Speed is incorrect.***
 
• **Velocity** is a **vector quantity** that represents the rate of change of **displacement**. While the instantaneous velocity of a moving body is non-zero, the **average velocity** over a closed path (where the object returns to the start) is **zero** because the total displacement is **zero**. However, displacement is the fundamental physical quantity that underpins this phenomenon. ***Hence, the statement regarding Velocity is partially contextual but displacement is the direct answer.***
 
• A classic example of **zero displacement** in motion is **circular motion**. When an athlete runs one full lap around a **circular track** and reaches the starting line, the **distance** covered is equal to the **circumference (2πr)**, but the **displacement** is **0**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Scalar vs. Vector Quantities:**

 
 
• **Scalar quantities** are those that have only **magnitude** and no **direction**. Examples include **distance**, **speed**, **mass**, and **time**.
 
• **Vector quantities** possess both **magnitude** and a specific **direction**. Examples include **displacement**, **velocity**, **acceleration**, and **force**.
 
 
 
• **Distance:**
 
 
• The **SI unit** for distance is the **meter (m)**.
 
• It is always **positive** or **zero** (if the body is at rest). It can never be **negative**.
 
• In any motion, the **distance** is always greater than or equal to the magnitude of **displacement**.
 
 
 
• **Displacement:**
 
 
• The **SI unit** is also the **meter (m)**.
 
• It can be **positive**, **negative**, or **zero** depending on the reference frame and direction of motion.
 
• It follows the laws of **vector addition**.
 
 
 
• **Velocity and Speed:**
 
 
• **Speed** is **distance/time**, while **Velocity** is **displacement/time**.
 
• The **SI unit** for both is **meters per second (m/s)**.
 
• If a body travels in a **straight line** without changing direction, the magnitude of **speed** and **velocity** are equal.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Uniform Circular Motion:** In this type of motion, the **speed** remains **constant**, but the **velocity** changes continuously because the **direction** of motion changes at every point. After **one complete revolution**, the **displacement** and **average velocity** are both **zero**.
 
• **Linear Motion:** If an object moves from point **A** to **B** and then moves back to point **C** (located between A and B), the **distance** is **AB + BC**, while the **displacement** is only the vector **AC**.
 
• **Dimensional Formula:** The dimensional formula for both **distance** and **displacement** is **[M0 L1 T0]**. For **speed** and **velocity**, it is **[M0 L1 T-1]**.
 
• **Practical Application:** In **GPS navigation** and **aviation**, understanding the difference between **displacement** (direct flight path) and **distance** (actual road or flight maneuvers) is crucial for **fuel calculation** and **time estimation**.

questions.question: The stem that undergoes modification, becomes flattened and carries chlorophyll to bear the responsibility of photosynthesis instead of leaf, is termed as ______________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Cladode**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **cladode** is a specialized **aerial stem modification** where the stem or branches become **flattened** or **cylindrical** and take over the **functions of a leaf**.
 
• These modified stems contain **chlorophyll** and are responsible for performing **photosynthesis**, a process usually reserved for leaves.
 
• In plants possessing cladodes, the **true leaves** are often reduced to **scales** or **spines** to minimize **water loss** through **transpiration**.
 
• Structurally, a **cladode** is generally limited to **one or two internodes** in length, distinguishing it from other similar modifications.
 
• Common biological **examples** of plants featuring cladodes include **Asparagus** and **Ruscus**, where these structures aid in survival in **arid** environments.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Rhizome**:

 
 
• A **rhizome** is a **thickened**, **prostrate**, **underground stem** that grows **horizontally**.
 
• It possesses distinct **nodes** and **internodes**, and it serves primarily as a **storage organ** for food and a means of **vegetative propagation**.
 
• Common examples include **Ginger (Zingiber officinale)**, **Turmeric**, and **Lotus**.
 
 
 
• **Stolon**:
 
 
• A **stolon** is a **sub-aerial stem modification** that originates as a **lateral branch** from the base of the main axis.
 
• It grows **aerially** for some time and then **arches downwards** to touch the soil, where it develops **adventitious roots** and a new **shoot** at the node.
 
• Examples include **Strawberry**, **Jasmine**, and **Wild Strawberry (Fragaria)**.
 
 
 
• **Thorn**:
 
 
• A **thorn** is a **hard**, **woody**, and **pointed** structure resulting from the modification of an **axillary bud**.
 
• Its primary **function** is to provide **protection** to the plant against **browsing animals** and **herbivores**.
 
• **Citrus** and **Bougainvillea** are well-known examples of plants that bear thorns.
 
 
 
• **Phylloclade**:
 
 
• A **phylloclade** is similar to a cladode but consists of **multiple nodes and internodes**.
 
• It is a **fleshy**, green stem found in **xerophytic plants** like **Opuntia (Cactus)**, where it stores **water** and performs **photosynthesis**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The modification of stems into **cladodes** and **phylloclades** is a vital **evolutionary adaptation** for plants living in **xeric (dry) habitats**.
 
• By shifting the **photosynthetic responsibility** from thin leaves to **fleshy stems**, the plant significantly reduces its **surface area** exposed to **evaporation**.
 
• In **Asparagus**, the **cladodes** appear in **clusters** and are often mistaken for leaves, while the actual **foliage leaves** are **non-photosynthetic scales** found at the base.
 
• Understanding these **morphological variations** is crucial in the study of **Plant Taxonomy** and **Botany** to identify species and their **ecological niches**.

questions.question: Which major mass movement did the Indian National Congress agree to withdraw, under the Gandhi–Irwin Pact of March 1931?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Civil Disobedience Movement**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Gandhi-Irwin Pact** was a landmark political agreement signed on **5 March 1931** between **Mahatma Gandhi**, representing the **Indian National Congress**, and **Lord Irwin**, the then **Viceroy of India**.
 
• Under the terms of this pact, the **Indian National Congress** agreed to discontinue the **Civil Disobedience Movement**, which had been active since **1930**.
 
• The **Civil Disobedience Movement** was a mass protest against the British **Salt Tax** and colonial laws, famously inaugurated with the **Dandi March** (Salt Satyagraha) from **12 March 1930** to **6 April 1930**.
 
• In return for withdrawing the movement, the British government agreed to release all **political prisoners** who were not accused of violence and allowed people living near the **sea coasts** to collect or manufacture **salt** for their own use.
 
• The pact also ensured that the **Indian National Congress** would participate in the **Second Round Table Conference** to be held in **London** later that year to discuss **constitutional reforms** for India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Non-Cooperation Movement (1920–1922):**

 
 
• Launched by **Mahatma Gandhi** after the **Rowlatt Act** and the **Jallianwala Bagh Massacre** of **1919**.
 
• It aimed to resist British rule through **non-violent** means such as boycotting **foreign goods**, **government schools**, and **courts**.
 
• The movement was abruptly called off in **February 1922** following the **Chauri Chaura** incident in **Uttar Pradesh**, where a violent mob set fire to a police station, killing **22 policemen**.
 
 
 
• **Quit India Movement (1942):**
 
 
• Also known as the **August Kranti**, it was launched at the **Bombay** session of the All-India Congress Committee on **8 August 1942**.
 
• Triggered by the failure of the **Cripps Mission**, it demanded an immediate end to British rule in India.
 
• **Mahatma Gandhi** gave the call of "**Do or Die**" (Karo ya Maro) during this movement.
 
 
 
• **Swadeshi Movement (1905–1911):**
 
 
• It was an economic strategy aimed at removing the British Empire from power and improving economic conditions in India by boycotting **British goods** and using **Indian-made products**.
 
• The movement was a direct consequence of the **Partition of Bengal** in **1905** by **Lord Curzon**.
 
• Key leaders included the **Lal-Bal-Pal** trio (**Lala Lajpat Rai**, **Bal Gangadhar Tilak**, and **Bipin Chandra Pal**).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **Gandhi-Irwin Pact** is often referred to as the **Delhi Pact**.
 
• The **Indian National Congress** formally endorsed the pact at its **Karachi Session** in **March 1931**, which was presided over by **Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel**.
 
• The pact was criticized by radical elements within the **Congress** and the youth because it did not secure the commutation of the death sentences of revolutionaries **Bhagat Singh**, **Rajguru**, and **Sukhdev**, who were executed on **23 March 1931**.
 
• The **Second Round Table Conference** (September–December **1931**) proved to be unsuccessful as the British government refused to grant **Purna Swaraj** (Complete Independence), leading to the resumption of the **Civil Disobedience Movement** in **1932**.

questions.question: After visiting India and learning about Indian culture, Al-Biruni wrote which book?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kitab-Ul-Hind**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Al-Biruni** was a renowned **Persian** scholar, polymath, and traveler who was born in **973 AD** in **Khwarizm** (modern-day **Uzbekistan**).
 
• He arrived in **India** in the **11th century** (specifically around **1017 AD**) accompanying **Mahmud of Ghazni** during his military expeditions.
 
• The book **Kitab-Ul-Hind** (also known as **Tahqiq-i-Hind**) was written by him in **Arabic**, providing a voluminous and lucid account of Indian life and culture.
 
• The work is divided into **80 chapters**, covering diverse topics such as **religion**, **philosophy**, **festivals**, **astronomy**, **alchemy**, **manners**, **customs**, **social life**, **weights**, **measures**, **iconography**, and **laws**.
 
• **Al-Biruni** adopted a unique methodology in his writing; he usually began each chapter with a **question**, followed by a description based on **Sanskrit** traditions, and concluded with a comparison to other cultures.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Babarnama**:

 
 
• This is the **autobiography** of **Zahir-ud-din Muhammad Babur**, the founder of the **Mughal Empire** in India.
 
• It was originally written in the **Chagatai Turkic** language during the **16th century**.
 
• The book provides detailed observations of the **flora**, **fauna**, **geography**, and **political landscape** of **Hindustan** and **Central Asia**.
 
 
 
• **Chahar Maqala**:
 
 
• Written by the Persian author **Nizami Aruzi** around **1156 AD**.
 
• The title translates to "**Four Discourses**," and it discusses four essential professions for a royal court: **secretaries**, **poets**, **astrologers**, and **physicians**.
 
• It serves as an important source of **literary history** and **Persian** courtly culture.
 
 
 
• **Qiran us Sa'dain**:
 
 
• This is a famous **Masnavi** (poem) composed by **Amir Khusrau** in **1289 AD**.
 
• The name means "**The Conjunction of the Two Auspicious Planets**," and it commemorates the historic meeting between **Sultan Muiz-ud-din Kaikubad** and his father **Nasir-ud-din Bughra Khan**.
 
• **Amir Khusrau** is often regarded as the "**Parrot of India**" for his contributions to Indo-Persian literature and music.
 
 
 
• **Language and Skills**: **Al-Biruni** was a linguist proficient in **Arabic**, **Persian**, **Hebrew**, **Syriac**, and **Sanskrit**. His mastery of **Sanskrit** allowed him to read the **Vedas**, **Puranas**, and the **Bhagavad Gita**, which heavily influenced the accuracy of **Kitab-Ul-Hind**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Indology**: Because of his objective and systematic study of Indian society, **Al-Biruni** is often called the "**Father of Indology**."
 
• **Caste System**: In **Kitab-Ul-Hind**, he provided a detailed analysis of the **Varna system**, attempting to explain the **caste hierarchy** while observing that similar divisions existed in ancient **Persia**.
 
• **Mathematics and Science**: He was deeply interested in the works of Indian mathematicians like **Brahmagupta** and **Varahamihira**. He accurately described the **Indian decimal system** and **astronomical theories** of the time.
 
• **English Translation**: The book was translated into **English** by the scholar **Edward Sachau** in **1888**, making this critical **11th-century** historical document accessible to the modern world.
 
• **Administrative and Geographic Insights**: He described the **land revenue** systems, the **topography** of the **Indo-Gangetic plain**, and the **river systems** of North India, which remains a primary source for historians studying the **medieval period**.

questions.question: Which of the following is not contained in Article 51?

options.text: Protection of forests and wildlife of India
Respect for international law and treaty obligations
Promotion of international peace and security
Just and honourable relations between nations

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Protection of forests and wildlife of India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 51** of the **Constitution of India** is a crucial provision under the **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP)**, located in **Part IV**. It specifically outlines the state's objectives regarding international relations and peace.
 
• The promotion of **international peace and security** is the primary goal of this article. It directs the **State** to endeavor to contribute to a peaceful global order. ***Hence, statement C is correct as it is contained in Article 51.***
 
• It mandates the maintenance of **just and honourable relations** between nations, emphasizing mutual respect and ethical conduct in diplomacy. ***Hence, statement D is correct as it is contained in Article 51.***
 
• The article further fosters **respect for international law** and **treaty obligations** in the dealings of organized peoples with one another. ***Hence, statement B is correct as it is contained in Article 51.***
 
• It also encourages the **settlement of international disputes** through the process of **arbitration** rather than conflict.
 
• **Protection of forests and wildlife of India** is not a part of **Article 51**. This objective is actually enshrined in **Article 48A**, which deals with the protection and improvement of the environment. ***Hence, statement A is incorrect (not contained in Article 51).***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP):**

 
 
• These principles are covered under **Articles 36 to 51** in **Part IV** of the Indian Constitution. They are **non-justiciable** in nature, meaning they cannot be enforced by a court of law, but they are fundamental in the governance of the **country**.
 
• The concept of DPSP was borrowed from the **Irish Constitution**.
 
• **Article 51** specifically represents the **Liberal-Intellectual** category of these principles, reflecting India’s commitment to global cooperation.
 
 
 
• **Environment Protection and Article 48A:**
 
 
• **Article 48A** was added to the Constitution through the **42nd Amendment Act of 1976**.
 
• It states that the **State** shall endeavor to protect and improve the **environment** and to safeguard the **forests** and **wildlife** of the country.
 
• This amendment was a significant step in establishing ecological conservation as a constitutional priority in **India**.
 
 
 
• **Fundamental Duties (Article 51A):**
 
 
• While **Article 51** focuses on the State's duty toward international peace, **Article 51A(g)** imposes a **Fundamental Duty** on every citizen to protect and improve the natural environment including **forests, lakes, rivers, and wildlife**.
 
• This duty was also inserted by the **42nd Amendment Act** in **1976** upon the recommendation of the **Swaran Singh Committee**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The 42nd Amendment Act, 1976:** This is often called the **"Mini-Constitution"** due to the vast number of changes it introduced. It notably expanded the scope of DPSPs by adding **Article 39A, Article 43A, and Article 48A**.
 
• **International Context:** Article 51 aligns with the principles of the **United Nations Charter**. It has historically served as the constitutional foundation for India’s **Non-Aligned Movement (NAM)** policy and the **Panchsheel** principles (Five Principles of Peaceful Coexistence) signed in **1954**.
 
• **Legal Status:** Unlike **Fundamental Rights**, if the State fails to implement **Article 51**, a citizen cannot file a **writ petition** in the **Supreme Court** or **High Court**. However, the **judiciary** often uses these principles to interpret laws and the scope of Fundamental Rights.

questions.question: The mean of 80 numbers was found to be 49. If at the time of calculation, two numbers were incorrectly taken as 69 and 74 instead of 92 and 83, then the correct mean is _____.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

⇒ Wrong sum = 49 × 80 = 3920

⇒ Correction = (92 + 83) − (69 + 74) = 175 − 143 = 32

⇒ Correct sum = 3920 + 32 = 3952

⇒ Correct mean = 3952 ÷ 80 = 49.4

**∴ Answer = 49.4**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Mean = 49, Total numbers = 80

Wrong numbers = 69, 74

Correct numbers = 92, 83

**Concept Used:**

Mean = Total sum ÷ Number of observations

**Calculation:**

⇒ Wrong total sum = 49 × 80 = 3920

⇒ Sum of wrong values = 69 + 74 = 143

⇒ Sum of correct values = 92 + 83 = 175

⇒ Correction = 175 − 143 = 32

⇒ Correct total = 3920 + 32 = 3952

⇒ Correct mean = 3952 ÷ 80 = 49.4

**∴ The correct answer is 49.4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

**Mean Formula:** Mean = Sum ÷ Number

**Error Correction:** Replace wrong values with correct ones

**Shortcut Idea:** Add net difference directly

**Exam Tip:** Always adjust total sum, not mean directly

questions.question: In a cricket match, a team needs 300 runs in 50 overs to win. In the first 15 overs, the team scores at an average rate of 5 runs per over. In the next 15 overs, the scoring rate improves to 8 runs per over. In the following 10 overs, the rate drops to 4 runs per over. What should be the run rate per over required in the remaining overs to win the match?
questions.solution:
